answers.title: In a dev daemon
answers.text: The dev window is open (title and status show dev-check-voice-mode, scratch repo, Overseer view). The first window opened transparent and click-through (the test harness's background launch reached owner checks); it was reopened as a normal window and scripts/dev was fixed so owner checks never use it.

answers.title: Turn it on
answers.text: Voice Mode turned on after the model download and heard 'How's it going, Overseer?' correctly (request went to Overseer, no agent). Bugs found and fixed in the dev build: the dev instance lacked the listener; dictation (Wispr Flow, CoreSpeech) paused it as a call; a stale pause survived a listener restart. Overseer's turn then failed on an expired sign-in (the owner signed in twice). Owner feedback: no visible button to turn it on; 'Show voice' should become the home page turning into the voice view with animation; the voice choice is odd though clear; the request id 'V-0001' means nothing to a user; the line 'Stop, mute and what's running still work' is unneeded; Overseer should reason and talk back, not only dispatch.

answers.title: Mute
answers.text: Yes: the orange microphone dot went off within a second of muting and came back on unmute. Separately, a natural follow-up (no 'Overseer', no command verb) was heard and transcribed but not sent: the local gate kept it as context. Owner wants follow-ups right after an answer to count.

answers.title: The mark
answers.text: The star moves with talking. It also moves for coughs, and sometimes for desk taps, so noise is not fully filtered (AC-177's 'stays at rest' not met). Owner: noise filtering should be an optional checkbox.

answers.title: A quiet room
answers.text: Ten minutes of ordinary work with a video playing: two false requests from non-speech sounds. A burp became 'Go!' (V-0004, answered by Overseer), and a throat clear became 'and move.' (V-0005, left waiting and cancelled). Otherwise nothing, which the owner found not bad overall. Single command words heard from noise are sent (see AC-222). Also: Voice Mode lowered YouTube's volume while listening (macOS voice-processing ducking).

answers.title: Echo on speakers
answers.text: Worked perfectly: on speakers it answered 'what's running?' aloud without hearing itself, and 'Overseer, stop' stopped it at the end of the phrase.

answers.title: VS Code closed
answers.text: Yes: with the dev VS Code quit, 'Overseer, what's running?' was answered aloud (both agents done and inactive).

answers.title: The session
answers.text: The owner's verdict: it did not fit their whole use case yet. It did not open the finished work when asked; it was hard to get it to show the agent; it should move the owner around VS Code (focus the agent asked about, open its chat or review, open the finished work). 2026-09-28, about 19:05-19:50, personal Claude on Haiku, two scratch repos (overseer-site, overseer-notes). Worked: agents started by voice in the named repo; Overseer asked a clarifying question ('what does rebuild refer to?') and took the follow-up; check-ins reported the agent done; echo and stop were solid earlier. Did not work: a clear request was judged 'not for Overseer' by the model; 'On it' was followed by 'not for Overseer'; 'repo' heard as 'rebuild' and 'sections' as 'actions', so the agent built the wrong thing with no read-back; no action to set an agent's permission mode ('auto mode' became a failed cadence change, raw error shown); a waiting permission did not come up by itself; after 'On it' nothing visible happened; Needs you did not clear when the agent was done; 'show me it' gave a relative path; the review showed 0 files and no diff for the agent's committed file, Save looked like accepting; Open PR on a repo with no remote gave a macOS alert. Friction and wishes: combine Voice Mode and Talk to Overseer into one view (Needs you inside it); slide the view aside to show a single started agent (with a setting to not auto-focus); cards take you to the agent or its work; open or edit an agent's worktree in place (a Follow option, Manual edit, with the agent's edits annotated); Overseer may set agents to Auto on its own. Only three agents in two repositories was not reached: one agent started.

steps.title: In a dev daemon
steps.do: Nothing to do: the runner started a dev daemon and an isolated dev VS Code built from main, beside your installed Overseer, and opened the Overseer view with two fixture agents in a scratch repository.
steps.watch: The window's title starts with [dev-check-voice-mode] and its status bar reads "Overseer dev-check-voice-mode". Your own VS Code is unchanged.
steps.record: Is the dev window open as described, and your own VS Code untouched?

answer.title: In a dev daemon
answer.text: The dev window is open (title and status show dev-check-voice-mode, scratch repo, Overseer view). The first window opened transparent and click-through (the test harness's background launch reached owner checks); it was reopened as a normal window and scripts/dev was fixed so owner checks never use it.

steps.title: Turn it on
steps.do: In the dev window press ⌘⌥⇧V (Overseer: Voice Mode: Turn On or Off). Accept the speech model download (small.en, 465 MiB, once). When macOS asks for the microphone, read the prompt, then Allow.
steps.watch: The prompt must name Overseer Listener.
steps.record: What did the microphone prompt say, and did Voice Mode turn on?

answer.title: Turn it on
answer.text: Voice Mode turned on after the model download and heard 'How's it going, Overseer?' correctly (request went to Overseer, no agent). Bugs found and fixed in the dev build: the dev instance lacked the listener; dictation (Wispr Flow, CoreSpeech) paused it as a call; a stale pause survived a listener restart. Overseer's turn then failed on an expired sign-in (the owner signed in twice). Owner feedback: no visible button to turn it on; 'Show voice' should become the home page turning into the voice view with animation; the voice choice is odd though clear; the request id 'V-0001' means nothing to a user; the line 'Stop, mute and what's running still work' is unneeded; Overseer should reason and talk back, not only dispatch.

steps.title: Mute
steps.do: Press ⌘⌥⇧M, watch the menu bar, then press ⌘⌥⇧M again to unmute.
steps.watch: The orange microphone dot in the menu bar goes off within a second of muting.
steps.record: Did the dot go off within a second, and come back on unmute?

answer.title: Mute
answer.text: Yes: the orange microphone dot went off within a second of muting and came back on unmute. Separately, a natural follow-up (no 'Overseer', no command verb) was heard and transcribed but not sent: the local gate kept it as context. Owner wants follow-ups right after an answer to count.

steps.title: The mark
steps.do: Press ⌘⌥V to show the voice view. Talk normally for a bit; then tap the desk, type and cough without talking.
steps.watch: The star grows and swings with your voice, and stays at rest for the taps, typing and cough.
steps.record: How did the star move with your voice, and did it stay at rest for the other sounds?

answer.title: The mark
answer.text: The star moves with talking. It also moves for coughs, and sometimes for desk taps, so noise is not fully filtered (AC-177's 'stays at rest' not met). Owner: noise filtering should be an optional checkbox.

steps.title: A quiet room
steps.do: Ten minutes of ordinary work (typing, moving, a video playing) with Voice Mode on, without talking to Overseer.
steps.watch: No request is made and nothing interrupts you.
steps.record: Over the ten minutes, was there any request or interruption?

answer.title: A quiet room
answer.text: Ten minutes of ordinary work with a video playing: two false requests from non-speech sounds. A burp became 'Go!' (V-0004, answered by Overseer), and a throat clear became 'and move.' (V-0005, left waiting and cancelled). Otherwise nothing, which the owner found not bad overall. Single command words heard from noise are sent (see AC-222). Also: Voice Mode lowered YouTube's volume while listening (macOS voice-processing ducking).

steps.title: Echo on speakers
steps.do: On speakers, not headphones, say "what's running?". While Overseer answers, say "Overseer, stop".
steps.watch: Overseer answers aloud and its own voice does not come back as a request; it stops at the end of the phrase after "Overseer, stop".
steps.record: Did it answer aloud without hearing itself, and stop at the end of the phrase?

answer.title: Echo on speakers
answer.text: Worked perfectly: on speakers it answered 'what's running?' aloud without hearing itself, and 'Overseer, stop' stopped it at the end of the phrase.

steps.title: VS Code closed
steps.do: Quit the dev VS Code window (⌘Q in it; not your own VS Code) and say "Overseer, what's running?".
steps.watch: It answers aloud with VS Code closed.
steps.record: Did it answer aloud with the dev VS Code closed?

answer.title: VS Code closed
answer.text: Yes: with the dev VS Code quit, 'Overseer, what's running?' was answered aloud (both agents done and inactive).
